pages:
I found this record among the remaining writings of Myrath.

It was written by one of the councillors during the final days of the kingdom.

Unlike the other records, this one was not hidden.

It was left inside the council chamber.

As though the writer expected someone to find it.

THE COUNCILLOR'S RECORD

Valdren has finally arrived.

They brought everything they discovered.

Everything they saw in Eldoria.

Everything they learned about Ashenreach.

Their spies had been watching the other kingdoms for years, but what they told us today was different.

They spoke of Eldoria.

They spoke of the disappearance.

They spoke of people returning from those lands who were no longer themselves.

They told us that something was there.

Something they could not understand.

Something far more dangerous than anything we had prepared for.

They believe Ashenreach is responsible.

They believe the power they found is connected to everything that happened.

And now we know enough.

We cannot sit and wait.

If Ashenreach is allowed to continue...

there may be nothing left.

So we prepare for war.

Our warriors have gathered.

Our weapons are ready.

Valdren will stand with us.
Tomorrow, we march.

Something is wrong.

The day has come.

The armies are ready.

The weapons have been prepared.

But Valdren...

is gone.

No message.

No warning.

Nothing.

We searched for them.

Their camps are empty.

Their people are gone.

Their spies never arrived.

It is the same thing that happened to Eldoria.

Whatever took them...

knows too much.

I asked the soldiers if anyone had seen them leave.

Nobody had.

One of the scouts said something strange.

He said there were footprints outside the camp.

Hundreds of them.

All leading toward the forest.

None leading back.

We followed them.

They stopped at the edge of the trees.

There was nothing beyond them.

No bodies.

No weapons.

No sign of a struggle.

Only one thing remained.

A piece of stone.

It carried the same symbol found in the old records.

We left it there.

We did not touch it.

Only Myrath and Ashenreach remain.

There is no turning back.

Our scouts report that Ashenreach has gathered their forces.

They are different now.

Even from a distance, something about them seems wrong.

Their armour has changed.

Their weapons have changed.

Some of them do not appear to breathe.

I asked the scouts if they were certain.

They were.

One of them refused to go back.

He said the soldiers were watching him.

I told him soldiers watch the enemy.

He said they were not looking at him.
They were looking behind him.

The battle has begun.

I have never seen anything like this.

Ashenreach has become something else.

Their soldiers fight with a power I cannot understand.

Our warriors are falling.

But they refuse to stop.

They fight with everything they have.

I should be with them.

I should be fighting.

But I am afraid.

So I stayed behind.

I can hear the battle from here.

Steel.

Fire.

Screaming.

Then silence.

Then more screaming.

Something is wrong.

The soldiers are saying the same thing.

They say there is something on the battlefield.

Something that is not Ashenreach.

Something that is not Myrath.

It is simply...

there.

The battle has stopped.

Nobody knows why.

Ashenreach has stopped attacking.

Our warriors have stopped advancing.

They are all looking toward the centre of the battlefield.

I cannot see what they are looking at.

There is smoke everywhere.

One of the soldiers came to the council chamber.

He was covered in blood.

Not his own.

He said the enemy had disappeared.

I asked him where they went.

He said:

"They didn't."

I asked what he meant.

He would not answer.

Then he asked me something.

"Did you see it?"

I told him no.

He began to cry.

There is something outside.

I can hear footsteps.

Slow.

Heavy.

They stop outside the chamber.

Nobody speaks.

Nobody moves.

The door has not opened.

But there is a shadow beneath it.

It does not belong to anyone standing outside.

It is moving.

I have ordered everyone to remain silent.

The shadow has stopped.

I think...

it is listening.

The door is still closed.

The shadow is gone.

We waited for hours.

Nothing happened.

Then one of the warriors opened the door.

There was nobody there.

Only a mark on the ground.

The same symbol.

Again.

Always the same symbol.

I am beginning to understand.

Ashenreach did not create this.

Eldoria did not discover it.

Valdren did not uncover it.

We have only been following its trail.

Perhaps it was here long before us.

Perhaps it was here before the kingdoms.

Perhaps it was here before anyone remembers.

The battlefield is empty.

Ashenreach is gone.

Their soldiers.

Their king.

Everything.

We searched the ruins.

There are no survivors.

No bodies.

No weapons.

Nothing.

Myrath is almost empty too.

The remaining warriors have begun leaving.

They believe there is nothing left to fight.

They are wrong.

There is still something here.

I can feel it.

I do not know how else to describe it.

It feels as though the kingdom itself is being watched.

I found the old records tonight.

The ones the elders told us never to open.

I opened them.

I wish I hadn't.

The oldest pages do not mention Ashenreach.

Or Eldoria.

Or Valdren.

Or Myrath.

They speak of the people who lived here before all of us.

The people who built the first ruins.

The people whose names have been forgotten.

And they mention the same thing.

The same symbol.

The same warning.

The same...

presence.

There is one line that has been written again and again.

I have copied it below.

IT DOES NOT COME WHEN CALLED.

IT COMES WHEN FOUND.

I understand now.

The kingdoms thought they were searching for power.

Ashenreach searched for it.

Eldoria searched for answers.

Valdren searched for the truth.

Myrath searched for someone to blame.

But none of us were searching for the right thing.

We were searching for something that had already found us.

I can hear something outside again.

This time there are no footsteps.

No shadow.

Nothing.

Just silence.

Too much silence.

The guards have stopped speaking.

I went to check on them.

They were standing in the courtyard.

All of them.

Looking upward.

I asked what they were looking at.

Nobody answered.

Then one of them pointed toward the ruins.

There was a light.

I have seen it before.

The same light described in the old records.

The same light found beside the darkness.

It is here.

After all this time...

it is here.

If anyone finds this record...

do not search for the power.

Do not search for the ruins.

Do not search for the thing beneath them.

Leave this place.

Forget the names of the kingdoms.

Forget what happened here.

And whatever you do...

do not look for the Temple.

MY NOTES

The councillor never finished the record.

There are no more pages.

I searched through what remained of Myrath.

But there is almost nothing left.

The ruins are gone.

The houses.

The roads.

The walls.

Even the old stones I had spent years studying...

gone.

In their place stands an arena.

I do not know who built it.

I do not know when it appeared.

I am certain it was not here before.

I remember these ruins.

I walked through them.

I searched their houses.

I slept beneath their broken walls.

Now there is nothing.

Only the arena.
And I am beginning to think the presence has been following me.

I found more records.

More than I have written here.

Far more.

They speak of Ashenreach.

One line was repeated several times:
"We wanted power. We found something that wanted us."

They speak of Eldoria too.

One of the elder's notes reads:
"Sometimes, the more knowledge we gain, the less we understand."

Another says:

"Perhaps some knowledge is not meant to be known."

There are records of Valdren.

Records of their spies.

Their warnings.

Their attempts to understand what was happening.

And records of Myrath.

Their final battles.

Their final days.

Their final mistake.

I have not copied everything.

I do not think I should.

Some of the records contain things I cannot explain.

Some names appear where no names should.

Some pages describe places I have never visited.

Yet I recognize them.

I have seen them.

I have walked through them.

There is something else.

The records do not end with the kingdoms.

They continue.

Someone kept writing.

Long after Ashenreach disappeared.

Long after Eldoria went silent.

Long after Valdren and Myrath were gone.

I do not know who wrote them.

I do not know how they survived.
And I do not know why they seem to be describing things that have not happened yet.
I found one page with only a single sentence.
"He is getting closer."

I do not know who he is.

But I have stopped searching for the answer.

For now.

There is one place I need to see.

The Temple of God.

The councillor only wrote a few words about it.

Nothing that explains what it is.

But if these arenas are really testing whoever enters them...

then perhaps there is a reason they still remain.

Perhaps the kingdoms were not destroyed simply because they were greedy.

Perhaps the arenas were not built as memorials.
Perhaps they were built for a purpose.

I have spent years searching for the truth.

I have followed the ruins.

The records.

The symbols.

The kingdoms.

And now...

I know where I am going next.
The Temple of God.
